verses.saheeh: I swear by the Day of Resurrection
verses.khattab: I do swear by the Day of Judgment
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nay! (the lā is extra in both instances) I swear by the Day of Resurrection.
verses.romanUrdu: Nahin main kasam khata hoon qayamat ke din ki

verses.saheeh: And I swear by the reproaching soul [to the certainty of resurrection].
verses.khattab: And I do swear by the self-reproaching soul
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And, nay, I swear by the (self-)reproaching soul, the one that reproaches itself, even if it should expend great effort in being virtuous (the response to the oath has been omitted, that is to say, la-tub‘athunna, ‘you shall indeed be resurrected!’, as indicated by [what follows]):
verses.romanUrdu: Aur nahin,main kasam khata hoon malamat karne wale nafs ki

verses.saheeh: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?
verses.khattab: Do people think We cannot reassemble their bones
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Does man, that is, [does] the disbeliever, suppose that We shall not assemble his bones?, for the raising [from the graves] and [for] the bringing back to life.
verses.romanUrdu: Kya Insan yeh samajh raha hai ke hum uski haddiyon ko jama na kar sakengey

verses.uthmani: بَلَىٰ قَٰدِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّىَ بَنَانَهُۥ
verses.indopak: بَلٰى قٰدِرِيۡنَ عَلٰٓى اَنۡ نُّسَوِّىَ بَنَانَهٗ
verses.saheeh: Yes. [We are] Able [even] to proportion his fingertips.
verses.khattab: Yes ˹indeed˺! We are ˹most˺ capable of restoring ˹even˺ their very fingertips
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Yes, indeed!, We shall assemble them. We are able, in addition to assembling them, to reshape [even] his fingers, that is to say, to restore their bones just as they had been, despite their smallness: so how much more so [are We able to restore] the larger ones!
verses.romanUrdu: Kyun nahin? Hum to uski ungliyon ke por por tak theek bana dene par qadir hain

verses.saheeh: But man desires to continue in sin.
verses.khattab: Still people want to deny what is yet to come
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nay, but man desires to deny (li-yafjura: the lām is extra, and the subjunctive mood is because of an implied [preceding] an, ‘that’) what lies ahead of him, namely, the Day of Resurrection, as is indicated by:
verses.romanUrdu: Magar Insan chahta yeh hai ke aagey bhi badh-aamaliyan karta rahey

verses.saheeh: He asks, "When is the Day of Resurrection?"
verses.khattab: asking ˹mockingly˺, “When is this Day of Judgment?”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿He asks, ‘When is the Day of Resurrection?’ — the question is meant in mockery and denial.
verses.romanUrdu: “Puchta hai” aakhir kab aana hai woh qayamat ka din

verses.saheeh: So when vision is dazzled
verses.khattab: But when the sight is stunned
verses.jalalayn: ﻿But when the eyes are dazzled (read bariqa or baraqa), startled and perplexed upon seeing some of those things which it used to deny;
verses.romanUrdu: Phir jab dedhey pathra jayengey (sight is dazed)

verses.saheeh: And the moon darkens
verses.khattab: and the moon is dimmed
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and the moon is eclipsed, darkening, its light disappearing,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur chand be-noor ho jayega

verses.saheeh: And the sun and the moon are joined,
verses.khattab: and the sun and the moon are brought together
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and the sun and the moon are brought together, so that both of them will rise from the west; or [it means when] the light of both of them disappears — and this will be on the Day of Resurrection —
verses.romanUrdu: Aur Chand Suraj mila kar ek kardiya jayenge

verses.saheeh: Man will say on that Day, "Where is the [place of] escape?"
verses.khattab: on that Day one will cry, “Where is the escape?”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿on that day man will say, ‘Where is the escape?’
verses.romanUrdu: Us waqt yahi Insan kahega kahan bhaag kar jaun

verses.saheeh: No! There is no refuge.
verses.khattab: But no! There will be no refuge
verses.jalalayn: ﻿No indeed! — a deterrent against seeking to escape — There is no refuge, no shelter to seek protection in.
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin,wahan koi jaye panaah na hogi

verses.saheeh: To your Lord, that Day, is the [place of] permanence.
verses.khattab: On that Day all will end up before your Lord
verses.jalalayn: ﻿On that day the recourse will be to your Lord, the [final] recourse of all creatures, whereupon they will be reckoned with and requited.
verses.romanUrdu: Us roz terey Rubb hi ke samney jaakar theharna hoga

verses.uthmani: يُنَبَّؤُا۟ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ يَوْمَئِذٍۭ بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ
verses.indopak: يُنَبَّؤُا الۡاِنۡسَانُ يَوۡمَٮِٕذٍۢ بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَاَخَّرَ ؕ
verses.transliteration: yunabbao alinsanu yawmaithin bima qaddama waakhkhara
verses.saheeh: Man will be informed that Day of what he sent ahead and kept back.
verses.khattab: All will then be informed of what they have sent forth and left behind
verses.jalalayn: ﻿On that day man will be informed of what he has sent ahead and left behind, [he will be informed] of the his first and last deeds.
verses.romanUrdu: Us roz Insan ko uska sab agla pichla kiya karaya bata diya jayega

verses.saheeh: Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness,
verses.khattab: In fact, people will testify against their own souls
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Rather man has insight into his [own] soul, for his limbs will speak of his deeds (the hā’ [sc. the tā’ marbūta in basīratun] is for hyperbole), and so he must be requited,
verses.romanUrdu: Balke Insan khud hi apne aap ko khoob janta hai

verses.saheeh: Even if he presents his excuses.
verses.khattab: despite the excuses they come up with
verses.jalalayn: ﻿though he should offer his excuses (ma‘ādhīr is the plural of ma‘dhira, but following a different pattern [from the usual ma‘dhira, ma‘ādhir]) that is to say, whatever excuse he offers will not be accepted from him.
verses.romanUrdu: Chahey woh kitni hi maazratein (excuses) karey

verses.uthmani: لَا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِۦ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِۦٓ
verses.indopak: لَا تُحَرِّكۡ بِهٖ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعۡجَلَ بِهٖ ؕ
verses.transliteration: la tuharrik bihi lisanaka lita'jala bihi
verses.saheeh: Move not your tongue with it, [O Muhammad], to hasten with recitation of the Qur'an.
verses.khattab: Do not rush your tongue trying to memorize ˹a revelation of˺ the Quran
verses.jalalayn: ﻿God, exalted be He, says to His Prophet: Do not move your tongue with it, with the Qur'an, before Gabriel is through with [reciting] it, to hasten it, fearing to lose it.
verses.romanUrdu: Aey Nabi , Is wahi ko jaldi jaldi yaad karne ke liye apni zubaan ko harkat na do

verses.saheeh: Indeed, upon Us is its collection [in your heart] and [to make possible] its recitation.
verses.khattab: It is certainly upon Us to ˹make you˺ memorize and recite it
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Assuredly it is for Us to bring it together, in your breast, and to recite it, your reciting of it, that is, its flowing off your tongue.
verses.romanUrdu: Isko yaad kara dena aur padhwa dena hamare zimmey hai

verses.saheeh: So when We have recited it [through Gabriel], then follow its recitation.
verses.khattab: So once We have recited a revelation ˹through Gabriel˺, follow its recitation ˹closely˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So, when We recite it, to you, by means of Gabriel’s recital, follow its recitation, listen to its recitation: thus the Prophet (s) would listen to it and then repeat it.
verses.romanUrdu: Lihaza jab hum isey padh rahey hon us waqt tum iske qirat ko gaur se sunte raho

verses.saheeh: Then upon Us is its clarification [to you].
verses.khattab: Then it is surely upon Us to make it clear ˹to you˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Then, it is for Us to explain it, by making you comprehend [it]: the connection between this verse and what preceded [it] is that those [verses before] imply turning away from God’s signs, whereas this one implies applying oneself to them by memorising them.
verses.romanUrdu: Phir iska matlab samjha dena bhi hamarey zimmey hai

verses.saheeh: No! But you love the immediate
verses.khattab: But no! In fact, you love this fleeting world
verses.jalalayn: ﻿No indeed! (kallā is for commencement, with the sense of alā) Rather you love the transitory [life], this world (both verbs [here and below] may be read in the second or third person plural),
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin, asal baat yeh hai ke tum log jaldi haasil honay wali cheez (yani duniya) se muhabbat rakhte ho

verses.saheeh: And leave the Hereafter.
verses.khattab: and neglect the Hereafter
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and forsake the Hereafter, thus neglecting to work towards [attaining bliss in] it.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur aakhirat ko chodh dete ho

verses.saheeh: [Some] faces, that Day, will be radiant,
verses.khattab: On that Day ˹some˺ faces will be bright
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Some faces on that day, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, will be radiant, fair and resplendent,
verses.romanUrdu: Us roz kuch chehrey tar-o-taza hongey

verses.saheeh: Looking at their Lord.
verses.khattab: looking at their Lord
verses.jalalayn: ﻿looking upon their Lord, in other words, they will see God, glorified and exalted be He, in the Hereafter.
verses.romanUrdu: Apne Rubb ki taraf dekh rahey hongey

verses.saheeh: And [some] faces, that Day, will be contorted,
verses.khattab: And ˹other˺ faces will be gloomy
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And other faces on that day will be scowling, glowering, frowning terribly,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur kuch chehrey udas hongey

verses.saheeh: Expecting that there will be done to them [something] backbreaking.
verses.khattab: anticipating something devastating to befall them
verses.jalalayn: ﻿certain that a spine-crushing calamity will fall on them, a great catastrophe, one that ‘crushes the spine’ (fiqār).
verses.romanUrdu: Aur samajh rahey hongey ke unke saath qamar-todh bartao hone wala hai

verses.saheeh: No! When the soul has reached the collar bones
verses.khattab: But no! ˹Beware of the day˺ when the soul reaches the collar bone ˹as it leaves˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿No indeed! (kallā: in the sense of alā) When it, the soul, reaches up to the collar bones,
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin, jab jaan halaq tak pahunch jayegi

verses.saheeh: And it is said, "Who will cure [him]?"
verses.khattab: and it will be said, “Is there any healer ˹who can save this life˺?”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and it is said, [and] those around him [the dying one] say: ‘Where is the enchanter?’, to perform incantations on him and cure him,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur kaha jayega ke hai koi jhaad phook karne wala

verses.saheeh: And the dying one is certain that it is the [time of] separation
verses.khattab: And the dying person realizes it is ˹their˺ time to depart
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and he suspects, [he] the one whose soul has reached this [stage], that it is the [time of] parting, the parting with this world,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur aadmi samajh lega ke yeh duniya se judai ka waqt hai

verses.saheeh: And the leg is wound about the leg,
verses.khattab: and ˹then˺ their feet are tied together ˹in a shroud˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and the shank is intertwined with the [other] shank, that is, one of his shanks [will be intertwined] with his other shank at the moment of death; or [it means] the distress of parting with this world is intertwined with the distress of the arrival of the Hereafter;
verses.romanUrdu: Aur pindli(leg) se pindli(leg) judh jayegi

verses.saheeh: To your Lord, that Day, will be the procession.
verses.khattab: On that day they will be driven to your Lord ˹alone˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿on that day to your Lord will be the driving [of the souls] (al-masāq means al-sawq; this indicates the operator of the [above] idhā, ‘when’, the meaning being: ‘when the soul reaches the throat, it will be driven towards the judgement of its Lord’).
verses.romanUrdu: Woh din hoga tere Rubb ki taraf rawangi ka

verses.saheeh: And the disbeliever had not believed, nor had he prayed.
verses.khattab: This denier neither believed nor prayed
verses.jalalayn: ﻿For he, man, neither affirmed [the truth] nor prayed,
verses.romanUrdu: Magar usne na sach mana , aur na namaz padhi

verses.saheeh: But [instead], he denied and turned away.
verses.khattab: but persisted in denial and turned away
verses.jalalayn: ﻿but he denied, the Qur'an, and he turned away, from faith,
verses.romanUrdu: Balke jhutlaya aur palat gaya

verses.saheeh: And then he went to his people, swaggering [in pride].
verses.khattab: then went to their own people, walking boastfully
verses.jalalayn: ﻿then went off to his family swaggering, strutting about in self-conceit.
verses.romanUrdu: Phir akadta hua apne ghar walon ki taraf chal diya

verses.saheeh: Woe to you, and woe!
verses.khattab: Woe to you, and more woe
verses.jalalayn: ﻿[Woe be] nearer to you (there is a shift from the third [to the second] person address here; the term [awlā] is a noun of action, with the [following] lām being explicative, in other words, ‘what you are averse to is [now] near to you’) and nearer, that is because you are more deserving of it [woe] than anyone else,
verses.romanUrdu: Yeh rawish tere hi liye sazawaar hai aur tujh hi ko zeib deti hai

verses.saheeh: Then woe to you, and woe!
verses.khattab: Again, woe to you, and even more woe
verses.jalalayn: ﻿then [may woe be] nearer to you and nearer! — [repeated] for emphasis.
verses.romanUrdu: Haan yeh rawish tere hi liye sazawaar hai aur tujh hi ko zeib deti hai

verses.saheeh: Does man think that he will be left neglected?
verses.khattab: Do people think they will be left without purpose
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Does man suppose that he is to be left aimless?, left to his own devices without being obligated to the [prescribed] laws: let him not suppose that!
verses.romanUrdu: Kya Insan ne yeh samajh rakkha hai ke woh yunhi mohmal (left alone, unquestioned )chodh diya jayega

verses.uthmani: أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةًۭ مِّن مَّنِىٍّۢ يُمْنَىٰ
verses.indopak: اَلَمۡ يَكُ نُطۡفَةً مِّنۡ مَّنِىٍّ يُّمۡنٰى ۙ
verses.transliteration: alam yaku nu<u>t</u>fatan min maniyyin yumn<u>a</u>
verses.saheeh: Had he not been a sperm from semen emitted?
verses.khattab: Were they not ˹once˺ a sperm-drop emitted
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Was he not — that is, [indeed] he was — a drop of emitted semen? (read yumnā or tumnā) deposited into the womb.
verses.romanUrdu: Kya woh ek hakeer pani ka nutfa (sperm from semen) na tha jo (raham –e-madar mei) tapkaya jata hai

verses.saheeh: Then he was a clinging clot, and [Allah] created [his form] and proportioned [him]
verses.khattab: Then they became a clinging clot ˹of blood˺, then He developed and perfected their form
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Then it, the drop of semen, became a clot; then He, God, created, from it man, and proportioned [him], making the parts of his body upright,
verses.romanUrdu: Phir woh ek lothda(clot) bana, phir Allah ne uska jism banaya aur uske aazaa durust kiye

verses.saheeh: And made of him two mates, the male and the female.
verses.khattab: producing from it both sexes, male and female
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and made of it, of the drop of semen that became a blood-clot, then an embryo, a [small] mass of flesh, the two sexes, the two kinds, the male and the female, at times coming together and at times each being on their own.
verses.romanUrdu: Phir ussey mard aur aurat ki do qismein banayi

verses.uthmani: أَلَيْسَ ذَٰلِكَ بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يُحْۦِىَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ
verses.indopak: اَلَيۡسَ ذٰلِكَ بِقٰدِرٍ عَلٰٓى اَنۡ يُّحۡـىِۦَ الۡمَوۡتٰى
verses.saheeh: Is not that [Creator] Able to give life to the dead?
verses.khattab: Is such ˹a Creator˺ unable to bring the dead back to life
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Is not such, a Doer of [all] these things, able to revive the dead? — the Prophet (s) would say, ‘Yes, indeed!’
verses.romanUrdu: Kya woh ispar qadir nahin hai ke marne walon ko phir zinda karde
